paras: Why doing it myself worked better for me

Have I mentioned I'm a big fan of self-hypnosis? Doing it on my own seems far more useful than the very little I managed to do with a professional hypnotist. I was sober at the session and didn't feel especially suggestible, but I suspect that's not even the main reason the pro didn't work very well for me. The bigger issue was trust and precision.

fixes.what: scare quotes around professional (a sneer the published doesn't have)
he was sober at the hypnotist session, not now; and the larger issue was trust and precision
fixes.replace: I'm sober right now, and I don't feel especially suggestible, but I suspect that's not even the main reason the pro didn't work very well for me.
fixes.with: I was sober at the session and didn't feel especially suggestible, but I suspect that's not even the main reason the pro didn't work very well for me. The bigger issue was trust and precision.

paras: When I do it on my own, I can detect when the wording I'm using for a suggestion to my subconscious is slightly off, and talk to my subconscious to find out what it thinks is wrong with the wording. When I use an image, I can tell whether it's giving me useful information, or just telling me what I'm afraid of, or what I want to avoid, or what I want to be true, or something I don't understand yet. And I can notice my body saying no before my conscious mind talks me into a yes.

fixes.what: catching the body's no before the conscious mind argues itself into a yes
fixes.replace: or what I want to be true, or something else.
fixes.with: or what I want to be true, or something I don't understand yet. And I can notice my body saying no before my conscious mind talks me into a yes.

paras: A hypnotist working on me can't interact with my subconscious mind quickly enough to get the detailed feedback needed to know what's going on in my mind, since they aren't IN my mind. (Of course, there are advantages to having someone else guiding the process, since they may be able to see things I'm blind to, and can help me keep the process regulated and safe.) But doing it myself has one advantage nobody outside can copy: immediate dialogue with my own system.

fixes.with: since they aren't IN my mind.

paras: I found that especially amplified with loveyhuasca. My experiences included a much deeper understanding of my motivations, peaceful loving awareness operating alongside analytical clarity, the disappearance of unhelpful daydreaming, different priorities around relationships, stronger intuition, and repeated correction between intuition, subconscious response, and conscious analysis.
I also got stronger results when I practiced immediately after sky hypnosis:

Some benefits arrived the next morning or a few days later. After one loveyhuasca self-hypnosis session, I woke in what felt like an answer to prayer. I’d been dealing with a lot of lust energy and worrying it could pull me into a relationship that wasn’t right. I asked the subconscious to connect the heart chakra with the sacral chakra—to bring the love energy and sex energy into the same current. The next morning I woke in a kind of “perfected” love state. I didn’t feel that I needed to find a woman; the divine feminine felt somehow at zero distance from my heart. Ordinary interaction dissolved the state, but for a while it showed me a possibility my mind and heart may permit when the desire is sincere.

In the same vein, self-hypnosis seemed to extend a short chrunga trip for what felt like a long time, and it feels like if I needed to I could have continued for an arbitrary amount of time. Only because of life did I have to talk to people, etc. Phenomenologically, this is very important. Although I'm not recommending that anyone prolong an altered state forever, because it's better to integrate, etc.
